--- CRITICAL FINDINGS ---

[AUTH-1] Missing DB index on Project.userId
File: prisma/schema.prisma (L1-L1000)
Evidence: getProjects (actions/project.ts) queries db.project.findMany({ where: { userId } }) but the Project model in schema.prisma has no index or @@index on userId. This makes per-user project lookups require table scans as Project rows grow.  
Impact: At moderate-to-high scale, every projects listing becomes a full table scan causing DB CPU/io exhaustion and high latency for all authenticated requests.  
Fix: Add an index on userId (e.g., @@index([userId]) or a dedicated index field) and migrate so findMany WHERE userId hits the index.

[AUTH-2] Broken GitHub OAuth state → callback fails to bind user
File: src/app/api/github/auth/route.ts (L1-L220) and src/app/api/github/callback/route.ts (L1-L400)
Evidence: auth route generates state = crypto.randomUUID() and sets installUrl.searchParams.set('state', state) (state contains only a UUID), but callback reads const [stateValue, userId] = state.split(':') and rejects when userId is missing.  
Impact: OAuth/callbacks will frequently fail to associate the GitHub connection with the logged-in user, breaking repo/installation linking for all users and causing large numbers of failed connections at scale.  
Fix: Make the state encoding and decoding consistent (e.g., set state to `${state}:${userId}` or lookup pending state in the callback) and validate/expire states server-side.

[AUTH-3] Incorrect Prisma findUnique usage in auth checks (will throw)
File: actions/project.ts (L1-L220)
Evidence: Authorization checks use db.project.findUnique({ where: { id: projectId, userId: userId } }) and similar multi-field where clauses; Prisma findUnique expects a single unique identifier (or a correctly defined compound unique), so these calls will throw or behave incorrectly.  
Impact: Core resource authorization and requests will error (deny access) or crash under normal user flows, producing widespread auth failures as traf

--- CRITICAL FINDINGS ---

[AUTH-1] Missing DB index on Project.userId
File: prisma/schema.prisma (L1-L1000)
Evidence: getProjects (actions/project.ts) queries db.project.findMany({ where: { userId } }) but the Project model in schema.prisma has no index or @@index on userId. This makes per-user project lookups require table scans as Project rows grow.  
Impact: At moderate-to-high scale, every projects listing becomes a full table scan causing DB CPU/io exhaustion and high latency for all authenticated requests.  
Fix: Add an index on userId (e.g., @@index([userId]) or a dedicated index field) and migrate so findMany WHERE userId hits the index.

[AUTH-2] Broken GitHub OAuth state → callback fails to bind user
File: src/app/api/github/auth/route.ts (L1-L220) and src/app/api/github/callback/route.ts (L1-L400)
Evidence: auth route generates state = crypto.randomUUID() and sets installUrl.searchParams.set('state', state) (state contains only a UUID), but callback reads const [stateValue, userId] = state.split(':') and rejects when userId is missing.  
Impact: OAuth/callbacks will frequently fail to associate the GitHub connection with the logged-in user, breaking repo/installation linking for all users and causing large numbers of failed connections at scale.  
Fix: Make the state encoding and decoding consistent (e.g., set state to `${state}:${userId}` or lookup pending state in the callback) and validate/expire states server-side.

[AUTH-3] Incorrect Prisma findUnique usage in auth checks (will throw)
File: actions/project.ts (L1-L220)
Evidence: Authorization checks use db.project.findUnique({ where: { id: projectId, userId: userId } }) and similar multi-field where clauses; Prisma findUnique expects a single unique identifier (or a correctly defined compound unique), so these calls will throw or behave incorrectly.  
Impact: Core resource authorization and requests will error (deny access) or crash under normal user flows, producing widespread auth failures as traffic increases.  
Fix: Use findFirst/findMany with the where clause or define a compound unique key and use findUnique correctly; wrap with proper error handling to avoid runtime crashes.

--- WARNING FINDINGS ---

[AUTH-4] GitHub access tokens stored unencrypted in DB
File: src/app/api/github/callback/route.ts (L1-L400)
Evidence: Callback updates user with githubAccessToken: accessToken and includes a TODO comment "In production, you should encrypt this".  
Impact: Plain tokens in the DB lead to credential exposure on DB compromise and amplify blast radius for account takeover; at scale more tokens create a larger permanent sensitive store.  
Fix: Encrypt tokens at rest (KMS), rotate and store only short-lived tokens or move secrets to a secure vault, and limit token scope.

[AUTH-5] Clerk webhook user.created lacks idempotent upsert
File: src/app/api/webhook/clerk/route.ts (L1-L240)
Evidence: The clerk webhook handles user.created by calling db.user.create({ data: { id: id, ... } }) without upsert/dedupe; retries/duplicate events will cause unique constraint errors.  
Impact: Duplicate webhook deliveries (common at scale) will cause handler failures, missed user syncs, and potential webhook retry storms.  
Fix: Use db.user.upsert or catch unique-constraint errors and treat as idempotent (or dedupe via a WebhookEvent table like the GitHub handler).

[AUTH-6] Broad middleware bypass for /api/webhook paths
File: src/middleware.ts (L1-L120)
Evidence: Middleware explicitly returns early for any pathname starting with '/api/webhook' (and registers those paths as public routes).  
Impact: Any sensitive route accidentally placed under /api/webhook (or typos) will be unprotected by Clerk and open to unauthenticated access, increasing the attack surface at scale.  
Fix: Narrow public-route matcher to exact webhook endpoints and rely on per-route signature verification (already used) rather than a blanket auth bypass.

--- INFO ---

[AUTH-7] Provider & webhook hygiene observed
File: src/app/api/webhook/github/route.ts and src/app/api/webhook/dodo/route.ts
Evidence: GitHub webhook uses timing-safe HMAC verification and dedupes via webhookEvent.upsert; Dodo webhook uses standardwebhooks verification.
